Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

Implement drag-drop for upgrade cards from the market row onto eligible street businesses. Drag-drop = buy and play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, charges the +50% premium (matching business buy-and-place exactly).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Market upgrade cards registered as draggable (like business cards). Dragging shows premium label (50% extra cost).
- Street business slots registered as drop zones. Eligible slots highlight during drag (green), ineligible slots dim/flash red.
- Drop on eligible slot: `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand` executes (1 action, +50% premium), upgrade applied, drag-drop animation plays.
- Drop on ineligible slot: card snaps back to market, illegal-move feedback (shake + SFX), no action consumed.
- Action budget gating: drag-drop rejected when `actionsRemaining <= 0` (cursor disabled or visual feedback).
- Premium formula: `Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2` exactly matches business buy-and-place formula.

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — draggable upgrade cards, drop zones, premium label, highlight/feedback
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — drag-drop dispatch, legality gating

## Deliverables

- Draggable upgrade cards in renderer

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

# Intake Brief: Add a close business option to Main Street (CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV)

## Problem statement

In Main Street, a business/community-space card on the street grid can only be **sold**, which refunds 50% of purchase+upgrade cost and leaves the card **permanently on the grid** in an inert "sold" state — the slot stays occupied for the rest of the game (placement requires an empty slot). Players need a **Close** option: an action-consuming, coin-free action that **removes the card from the street entirely**, freeing the slot so a new card can be placed there later.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to replace an underperforming business instead of being stuck with a dead sold card in a key slot.

**Example user stories:**

- "As a player, I want to close a business that is losing money (negative ongoing cost) so I can place a better card in that slot on a later day."
- "As a player, I want to clear a community-space card from the street without keeping it as a permanently occupied slot."
- "As a player, I want a clear, confirmable way to close a street card (costing 1 action, no coins) distinct from selling it (free, refund, stays on the grid)."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope & UI (feature behavior):** During `MarketPhase`, every **non-sold** business and community-space card on the street grid offers a **Close** option; **sold** cards never do. The existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog (`showSellConfirmation`) is extended into a **Manage card** dialog with **[Sell] [Close] [Cancel]** buttons (reusing `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, HUD-container parenting, depth 199/200/201).
2. **Cost:** Closing consumes **exactly one daily action** via the shared `consumeAction` helper (`actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` decremented, floor 0 — CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) and grants **no coins**. Selling remains free and unchanged.
3. **Removal:** Closing removes the card from `streetGrid[slotIndex]` (slot → `null`), pushes it to the `discardPile` (not removed from the game), incrementally updates affected neighbors' cached income/synergy values, writes an activity-log entry, and the slot becomes **immediately placeable** by new cards.
4. **Undo & feedback:** Close is a **reversible command** (`closeBusinessCommand` via the undo manager restores the card, slot occupancy, action budget, and neighbor values) and is rendered with an **animation + SFX** consistent with the existing sell demolition (`animateSell`) and the event-driven audio rule (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).
5. **Quality & docs:** Unit tests cover legality (MarketPhase, non-sold, slot occupied, action sufficiency), cost, removal, neighbor recalculation, and undo; a browser test covers the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel); HUD/help tooltips and docs are updated (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` action-economy table: Close added under *action-consuming* operations, explicitly NOT in the "Free operations" list; GDD action-economy section; `ux-visual-audio.md` if the close animation differs); the **full test suite passes** (`npm test`) and the production build succeeds (`npm run build`).

## Constraints

- Action cost must go through the **single shared `consumeAction`** enforcement point (CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) — same path as `buyBusinessCommand`/`buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`; no double-decrement, no divergence.
- Follow the engine's existing patterns: `LegalityResult` discriminated union (`canCloseBusiness`), reversible `toCommand`/`snapshotAction` command, and `MainStreetMarket` action module structure mirroring `sellBusiness`/`canSellBusiness`.
- Modal dialog must follow the project's UI best practices (backdrop 199, box 200, interactive 201; parent all text/buttons into `hudContainer`; `dismissOverlay` cleanup) and SLL for positioning.
- Event-driven audio rule (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N-context rule in AGENTS.md): the close action must be animated and sounded via the shared helpers/SoundManager; `shakeIllegalMove`/illegal feedback for rejected closes; reduced-motion and mute/volume settings respected.
- i18n: dialog/label strings should follow the game's i18n pattern if the existing sell dialog strings are localized.
- Doc-update policy: this is a rules/mechanic change — `docs/main-street/*` must be updated in the same change; create a doc-update child work item if it can't land in the same commit.

## Existing state

- **Sell from street:** `sellBusiness` (`MainStreetMarket.ts`) marks `soldSlots[slotIndex] = true`, refunds `Math.ceil((purchasePrice + upgradeCosts) / 2)`, card stays on grid (inert — no income/synergy), **free** (no action consumed). Legality gate `canSellBusiness` (MarketPhase only, unsold only). `updateNeighborsOnSale` recalcs neighbors.
- **UI entry:** clicking a non-sold street card in `MarketPhase` → `MainStreetTurnController.onSellCard` → `MainStreetOverlayContent.showSellConfirmation` (Sell/Cancel, refund text) → `sellBusinessCommand` (free).
- **Placement:** `canPlaceFromHand` requires `streetGrid[slotIndex] === null` — so a sold card permanently occupies its slot today.
- **Engine legacy helper:** `sellFromTableau` already models "remove card entirely + to discard pile", but is unused by the street UI and prices at 75% (old PRD semantics) — NOT to be reused for Close (Close pays nothing).
- **AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` does not enumerate street sells (player-initiated); no AI changes expected, but verify — costs/empty-slot should not break AI budget tests (`ai-action-budget.test.ts`).
- **Docs:** `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` lists "Selling a business" under **Free operations**; Close must be added as an action-consuming op.

## Desired change

Add a **Close** action alongside Sell for street-grid cards: click a non-sold card → Manage card dialog ([Sell] [Close] [Cancel]); Close costs **1 action, no coins**, removes the card from the grid (slot → null), sends it to the discard pile, recalcs neighbors, logs the activity, animates + sounds the removal, and is undoable. Sold cards remain permanently on the grid (unchanged) and are not closeable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — add `closeBusiness()` + `canCloseBusiness()` (+ `CloseResult`) mirroring the sell helpers; neighbor recalculation (reuse `updateNeighborsOnSale`-style logic)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — add `closeBusinessCommand()` (consumes action via shared `consumeAction`; undo snapshot restores card/action/neighbors)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — extend `showSellConfirmation` into the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel) or add a parallel dialog
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — manage-card entry + close handler (legality, action-cost messaging, tutorial gating parity)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — street-card click/tooltip wiring (sold cards stay non-interactive; tooltip text)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — close removal animation + SFX (reuse/parallel `animateSell`)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — tooltip copy if the free-ops list changes (Close must not appear there)
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/` — localized strings for the new dialog if sell strings are localized
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — verify enumeration/budget unaffected (should be, like street sell)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts` (unit: legality, cost, removal, neighbors, undo) + a browser dialog test (or extend `MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` / `MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts`)
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (action-economy table), `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` (action economy), `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` (close animation), game help text/README if they describe street-card actions

## Related work

- CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC — shared `consumeAction` enforcement point (must be reused for Close's action cost)
- CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN — same-day composite buy-and-place pricing (context for the action economy; Close must not affect it)
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO — no turn-limit default (close-as-action fits the longer-horizon economy)
- CG-0MQVJ4DIC009K8D8 — Scenario Validation Test (critical; close legality must not break scenario validation)

**Related work (automated report — /skill:find-related):**

- **CG-0MM4RFN5N0KTUR66** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 5 -- Tutorial, Onboarding, and Game Selector Integration (completed; tutorial-gating context for the new dialog)
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — Main Street: merge business hand + held event into one horizontal 3-card hand (completed; hand/street interaction context)
- **CG-0MQK7IQE9003LH7X** — panel status lines not working (completed; overlay/panel polish context)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a closed card goes to the `discardPile` (consistent with `sellFromTableau`); it is not removed from the game, and it never returns to the market.
- **Risk — action economy:** Close is a new way to spend actions (effectively "demolish + refund-free sell" at the cost of 1 action). Monitor for degenerate play patterns (e.g., closing a card then immediately re-buying a better one each day); balance guardrails (`balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`) may need a follow-up review.
- **Risk — scope creep:** AI usage of Close, challenge interactions, tutorial/two-turn-step teaching updates, and stats/transcript schema changes are out of scope for this item — file follow-up work items if discovered during implementation.
- **Risk — sold-slot semantics:** sold cards permanently occupying slots is unchanged by this feature; a future "clear sold card" capability could be a separate work item.
- **Compatibility:** i18n coverage of new strings and browser-test interaction with tutorial gating must be checked; undo of Close must also restore the tutorial step state if gated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (action cost):** "Does 'costs nothing' mean a free operation (no coins AND no daily action, like sell), or does closing consume a daily action (like placing)?" — Answer (producer, via work-item review): **consume a daily action** (1 action point, no coins). Source: producer reply to intake questions comment, 2026-08-30.
- **Q2 (UI entry point):** "How does the player trigger a close?" — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — extend the existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog into a Manage card dialog with [Sell] [Close] [Cancel]. Source: producer reply, 2026-08-30.
- **Q3 (scope):** "Does Close apply to both business and community-space cards, and should sold (inert) cards be closeable?" — Answer (producer): **apply to all except sold** — both families are closeable; sold cards are not. Source: producer reply, 2026-08-30.
- **Q4 (discard) — noted assumption, not asked:** closed card → `discardPile` (slot → null, placeable). Open to revision if the producer prefers removal from the game.

# Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.
- The grid is **conceptually unbounded** (at minimum, support at least a 3×3 or 5×5 grid of streets). Practically, the grid could grow dynamically as the player zooms out further.
- Corner plots are **shared between streets**: one card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules (8-way Chebyshev) apply — the card counts as a neighbour to all adjacent slots across all streets it touches.
- The existing `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` constants and the flat 10-slot array must be refactored to support multi-street topology.
- Must preserve deterministic seed-based gameplay and save/load compatibility.

# Moving an event card should cost an action — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

In Main Street, moving an Investment event card from the market to hand is completely free (no action, no coins) and playing it from hand is also free (only the coin cost at play). Under the action economy (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R), business cards consume one action on move-to-hand and again on play-from-hand; events are the only card family that bypasses the daily action budget, effectively granting a free second action every day. Events should follow the same action economy as business cards: **move-to-hand = 1 action** and **play-from-hand = 1 action** (with a same-day composite costing 1 action total).

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — the one-action-per-day decision (1/day, 2 with General Manager) must apply uniformly; free event acquisition currently lets players stack multiple meaningful moves in a single day.
- **AI / Monte Carlo harness** — must budget event actions within the 1–2 action cap so simulations and the AI opponent behave like a constrained player.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need a consistent, testable action economy across engine, commands, controller, AI, and Monte Carlo.

### User Stories

- *"As a player, I want moving an event card to my hand to use my daily action, so the decision to acquire an event competes with placing a business."*
- *"As a player, I want to play a held event from a previous day to consume an action, so events follow the same economics as business cards."*
- *"As a player, I want moving and playing an event on the same day to count as a single action, so I'm not double-charged for a same-turn plan."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Move-to-hand consumes 1 action:** Clicking an Investment event in the market row moves it to hand and decrements `actionsRemaining`; legality gating rejects the move when the action budget is spent.
2. **Play-from-hand consumes 1 action:** Playing a held Investment event consumes 1 action and pays the event's listed coin cost (cost-at-play unchanged); gating rejects when the budget is spent. *(Merged from CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO.)*
3. **Same-day composite = 1 action total:** Moving an event to hand and playing that same-day-moved event costs a single action (move consumes it, same-day play is free), mirroring the business-card composite; playing a held event from a previous day costs 1 action.
4. **Coins unchanged:** Cost-at-play model preserved — no coins for the move; `event.cost` still deducted from `resourceBank.coins` when the event is executed.
5. **AI + Monte Carlo:** `MainStreetAiStrategy` and `MainStreetMonteCarlo` account for the event move/play action costs within the 1–2 action cap (budget-aware enumeration and scoring), and remain deterministic per seed.
6. **Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover action spend + gating for event move, event play, and the same-day composite; existing event/AI/MC tests updated; `npm test` and `npm run build` pass. *(Tutorial E2E depends on the out-of-scope tutorial rework CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N.)*
7. **Docs:** All related documentation updated (core rules & mechanics, card catalog, README); full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day, 2 while a General Manager is employed — events must not create an implicitly-free second action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business-card placement); the event composite mirrors the business-card move→place model.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields stay consistent (e.g. same-day composite tracking reuses `justMovedHandCardId`-style semantics).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.
- **Tutorial rework is OUT of scope** — tracked as blocking child CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N (T9/T20 depend on free event moves).

## Existing State

- `moveEventToHandCommand` (MainStreetCommands.ts:205) → `moveToHand` — **no** `consumeAction`.
- `playEventCommand` (MainStreetCommands.ts:233) → `playEventFromHand` — **no** `consumeAction`.
- Engine `executeAction` switch: `buy-event` → `purchaseEvent`, `play-event-from-hand`/`play-event` → `playEventFromHand` — none consume an action.
- `canPurchaseEvent` (MainStreetMarket.ts:162) gates only on hand capacity; comment: *"taking the event to hand is free"* (CG-0MT5W1V4D007NN8Q cost-at-play model).
- UI `onEventCardClick` (MainStreetTurnController.ts:~1113) and `onPlayHeldEvent` (~400) — no action-budget gating for events; success message says *"Moved event to hand (free)"*.
- AI `enumerateLegalActions`/`scoreEventAction` and Monte Carlo treat `buy-event`/`play-event` as free actions.
- Tutorial T9 explicitly assumes *"Events move to hand FREE (no action)"* to share day 2 with the Laundromat placement (T7); T20 plays the held Local Festival. (Out of scope → CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N.)

## Desired Change

Add event move/play to the action economy:

1. **Engine (`MainStreetEngine.ts`):** `executeAction` cases `buy-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, and `play-event` call `consumeAction(state)` before `purchaseEvent`/`playEventFromHand`.
2. **Commands (`MainStreetCommands.ts`):** `moveEventToHandCommand` and `playEventCommand` call `consumeAction` inside the snapshotted action (undo-safe).
3. **Market (`MainStreetMarket.ts`):** `canPurchaseEvent` gains an action-budget gate (or the gating lives at the command/controller layer — keep `canPurchaseEvent` in sync); add `canPlayEvent`-style legality for play if not already present.
4. **Turn controller (`MainStreetTurnController.ts`):** `onEventCardClick` / `onPlayHeldEvent` gate on `actionsRemaining`, spend the action, and implement the same-day composite (track the just-moved event id so same-day play is free).
5. **AI (`MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`):** budget-aware `enumerateLegalActions` (only event actions when budget > 0) and `scoreEventAction` updated for the action cost.
6. **Monte Carlo (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`):** event actions respect the 1–2 action cap; re-baseline if the harness has guardrails.
7. **UI feedback:** instruction text/state no longer claims events are free; action-counter dimming already reflects the budget.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `executeAction` switch: add `consumeAction` to `buy-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, `play-event`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `moveEventToHandCommand`, `playEventCommand`: add action spend
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `canPurchaseEvent` action gate; `purchaseEvent`, `playEventFromHand` untouched coin-wise
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — `onEventCardClick`, `onPlayHeldEvent`: gating, spend, same-day composite
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — same-day composite tracking (reuse `justMovedHandCardId` semantics or equivalent)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `enumerateLegalActions`, `scoreEventAction`: budget awareness
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — action-cap respect for event actions
- `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` — new/updated event action-spend tests
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` — cost-at-play tests (update only if cost semantics change — they don't)
- Tests: AI-strategy tests, Monte Carlo tests, save-load tests
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `example-games/main-street/README.md`
- **Out of scope (blocked):** `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts`, `TutorialScenario.ts`, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`, tutorial E2E parts — CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO** — "Executing an event in Main Street consumes an action" — **merged** into this item (closed as superseded, producer decision 2026-08-31).
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** — "Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)" — established move-to-hand and play-from-hand as actions for business cards; events were the leftover exception this item closes.
- **CG-0MT5W1V4D007NN8Q** — "Events in Main Street should be paid for when executed" — cost-at-play coin model; **unchanged** by this item.
- **CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP** — "Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first" — in progress; its "free ops unchanged" AC (events stay free) is now **conflicting** and must be updated (comment added).
- **CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N** — "Tutorial rework: event move/play now consume an action" — blocking child created at this intake.
- **CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2** — single-row market / hand rework (context).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Tutorial breakage (High):** T9 shares day 2 with the Laundromat placement on the assumption events move free. The tutorial E2E will fail once event moves consume an action — this is why the tutorial rework (CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N) is a blocking child. The parent's "full suite passes" AC is contingent on that child landing.
- **AI/Monte Carlo baseline shift (Medium):** with event actions budgeted, MC baselines may shift; re-baseline `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` and verify the harness rather than silently breaking it.
- **Same-day composite ambiguity (Medium):** the just-moved composite must match the business-card model exactly (move consumes the action; same-day play free) — do not double-charge a same-day move+play.
- **Upgrade-economy conflict (Medium):** CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP's plan AC still says event ops stay free; coordination needed when both land (comment posted).
- **Assumption — drag-and-drop parity:** events have no drag-drop buy-and-play path today (click-only), so no +50% premium model is introduced for events; composite only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** tutorial rework, coin-cost changes, and premium models for events are out of scope — recorded as linked work items (CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Should this item cover only the move, or both move AND play (merge with CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-31): "merge the two". Accepted: this item covers move-to-hand AND play-from-hand; CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO closed as superseded.
- Q2: "Same-day composite — move+play = 1 action total, or every play costs a separate action?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-31): "1 action". Accepted: same-day move+play composite = 1 action total; held-event play from a previous day = 1 action.
- Q3: "Tutorial rework in scope?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-31): "out of scope". Accepted: tracked as blocking child CG-0MTH3Z8ZB000MB8N; tutorial E2E gating is excluded from this item.
- Q4: "AI/Monte Carlo updates in scope?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-31): "in scope". Accepted: budget-aware enumeration/scoring for event actions in AI + MC.
- Q5: "Cost-at-play coins unchanged?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-31): "unchanged". Accepted: no coins for the move; `event.cost` still paid at execution.

# Core engine: charge an action for event move/play
Wire the event move/play paths into the existing Main Street action economy. Same-day composite mirrors the business-card model (move spends the action; same-day play of that just-moved event is free). Coins unchanged (no cost at move, `event.cost` at play).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `executeAction` cases `buy-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, and `play-event` call `consumeAction(state)` before delegating to `purchaseEvent`/`playEventFromHand`. Legality gating rejects event moves/plays when `actionsRemaining` is 0.
- [ ] `moveEventToHandCommand` and `playEventCommand` each call `consumeAction(state)` *inside* the snapshotted action body (undo-safe) and expose matching `canMoveEventToHand`/`canPlayEventFromHand` legality (action-budget gate).
- [ ] `canPurchaseEvent(state, ...)` rejects when hand capacity **or** `actionsRemaining ≤ 0`; `canPlayEvent(...)` (add if not already present) rejects under the same budget and additionally respects the same-day composite — playing the `justMovedHandCardId`-equivalent event on the same day does **not** double-charge.
- [ ] Same-day composite tracking: controller/engine reuse `justMovedHandCardId`-style semantics for events (set on move, checked on same-day play, cleared on end-turn/day reset). Playing a held event from a prior day costs 1 action; moving and playing the just-moved event costs 1 action total (no double charge).
- [ ] Controller/UI: `onEventCardClick` and `onPlayHeldEvent` gate on `actionsRemaining`, spend the single action for a composite via the command/engine path, and no longer claim events are free. Undo/redo reuses `UndoRedoManager` and invalidates the redo stack on new actions.
- [ ] `npm run build` and main-street unit tests pass; the one-child-per-task state regression coverage is unaffected.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want income to accrue only to the owning player of each placed business and shared events/incidents to retain their existing semantics routed per-owner, so the competitive economy is legible and testable.

## Context

`applyIncome` / adjacency income and `resolveEvent`/`resolveIncident` are single-player (one resourceBank/finalScore). Once street slots are owner-tagged (state-model sibling) and the phase machine delegates Income/Incident to per-owner handlers, the routing must be precise. Incident/Investment event regression risk: silent divergence where the wrong owner is credited or both are affected.

## Scope

- Per-owner income: each placed business's income (base + adjacency + upgrades + salary/ongoing) accrues only to its slot owner.
- Shared events/incidents: street-wide Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified (design within planning: per-owner effects vs. shared board effects).
- Single-player (N=1) income path unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Phase machine / win condition (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Income for each placed business accrues only to the owning player (verified by per-owner fixtures covering base + synergy + upgrade + salary/ongoing).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics and are routed per-owner as specified (design within planning); verified by per-owner event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic replay: same seed → identical per-owner income/event sequences.
- [ ] **AC4:** N=1 regression: income/event behaviour matches the pre-competitive single-player baseline.

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

# Do not show new market cards until turn has ended

## Problem statement

When the player clicks "End Turn", the market cards are cycled (old cards discarded, new cards dealt from deck) **immediately** inside `processEndOfTurn()`, before income calculation, incident resolution, and the 800ms delay. This leaves the player staring at newly dealt market cards while income/incident animations and log updates play out — a jarring disconnect where the player is looking at the next day's market before their current turn has finished resolving.

## Users

- **User story:** As a Main Street player, I want the market to stay unchanged during my turn's end-of-turn resolution (income, incidents, notifications) so I can see the full financial summary of the turn I just played.
- **User story:** As a player, I want the new market cards to appear only when the next day begins, giving me a clean visual transition between turns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Clicking "End Turn" no longer cycles the market cards. The old market cards remain visible during income calculation, incident resolution, and the income-feedback display.
- **AC2:** The market cards are cycled and refilled at the **start** of the next day (inside `startDayPhase()` / `executeDayStart()`), so the player sees the new market alongside the "Day N" transition banner.
- **AC3:** All existing unit tests pass, including `MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` and `staff-general-market-state.test.ts`. No regression in market cycling correctness.
- **AC4:** Tutorial gameplay is unaffected — scenario-placed market cards are still preserved across the day boundary as before.
- **AC5:** Competitive mode (multi-player) is unaffected — the same market-cycling behavior applies at the correct point in the closing phases.

## Constraints

- The `cycleMarketCards()` function itself is **not changed** — only its call site moves.
- The tutorial's `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` flag and related guard code can be **removed** since cycling no longer happens during end-of-turn processing.
- The market must still be refilled at day start — only the timing of the cycle changes (from end of old turn → start of new turn).

## Existing state

Market cards are cycled at the beginning of `processEndOfTurn()` in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
- **Line ~1430-1431** (single-player): `if (!state.skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn) { cycleMarketCards(state); }`
- **Line ~1212** (competitive): `if (!state.skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn) cycleMarketCards(state);`

Then income, incidents, and notifications play — the player sees the new cards during this wait.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** the `cycleMarketCards(state)` call from `processEndOfTurn()` (line ~1430-1431) and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` (line ~1212).
2. **Add** a `cycleMarketCards(state)` call in `executeDayStart()` right after the `refillMarket(state)` call (after line ~1264 in `MainStreetEngine.ts`). This ensures cycling happens at the start of each new day.
3. **Remove** the `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` state field, its guard in `processEndOfTurn()`, and its setting/clearing in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`.
4. The `executeCompetitiveDay` path (line ~1334) that calls `refillMarket` in `executeDayStart` already has a `skipMarketRefill` parameter — the new `cycleMarketCards` call should follow the same skip logic (skip on checkpoint resume).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Move `cycleMarketCards` from `processEndOfTurn()` and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` to `executeDayStart()`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Remove `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` guard in `endTurn()`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Remove `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` state field (~line 377)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` — Verify tests still pass (they call `cycleMarketCards` directly, so no change needed)
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Review if any scenario assumptions about market timing need updating

## Related work

- CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 — Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI (income/incident logging)
- CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ — Main Street log should show total effects (per-turn net summary)
- CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P — Tutorial: two-turn plan-ahead flow (uses `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` to preserve scenario cards)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The tutorial's `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` flag also suppresses cycling — removing it could cause scenario cards to be lost on end-turn. **Mitigation:** The cycle now happens in `startDayPhase()` which the tutorial already goes through, so scenario cards should still be preserved by `refillMarket()`'s top-up semantics (visible cards are preserved, only missing slots are drawn).
- **Assumption:** The `refillMarket()` top-up semantics (preserve visible cards, only draw into empty slots) correctly preserve scenario cards. If not, the scenario system may need an additional guard in `executeDayStart()`.
- **Scope creep:** This change only affects the timing of market cycling. No changes to market composition, card deal animations, or income calculation logic.
- **Assumption:** Competitive mode only calls `processEndOfTurn()` / `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` from `executeCompetitiveDay()`, which in turn calls `executeDayStart()` for the next day — the new cycle location applies uniformly.

## Goal (user story)

As a player who just reached the win threshold in endless mode, I want an "Enter Endless Mode" button on the end-game dialog so I can continue playing beyond the threshold.

## Context

CG-0MTIILU5V006GCN4 wired the endless-mode logic: when `config.endlessMode === true` and a player reaches the score threshold, the engine sets `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and keeps `gameResult = 'playing'`. The end-game dialog (`MainStreetOverlayContent.showGameOverOverlay`) already reads `endReason` for display, but the player has no way to actually continue — the only options are "Play Again" (restart) and "Menu" (quit). This leaves the endless-mode feature inert from a player-facing perspective.

## Scope

- Add an "Enter Endless Mode" button to the end-game dialog when `endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- When pressed, the button dismisses the overlay and resumes gameplay from the current state (no restart).
- The button is hidden in all other end-reasons (normal win, bankruptcy, turn exhaustion, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Competitive mode endless mode (separate CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 children).
- UI changes to the main menu or difficulty selector.
- Any Monte Carlo or AI changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** End-game dialog shows an "Enter Endless Mode" button when `state.endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- [ ] **AC2:** Pressing the button dismisses the game-over overlay, resets `endReason` to `null` (or appropriate continuation value), and resumes the game loop — the game continues playing and scoring.
- [ ] **AC3:** The button is not shown when `endReason` is anything other than `score_threshold_continue`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showGameOverOverlay()` adds the button.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Resume logic after button press (dismiss overlay, call engine continuation).
- `tests/main-street/` — New or updated tests covering button appearance/dismiss/resume.

## Target Outcome
Deterministic, fast unit tests prove `BankingGreedyStrategy` deliberately hoards vs spends correctly and respects legality, before implementation lands.

## Definition of Done
- Suite imports `BankingGreedyStrategy` (name === 'BankingGreedy', implements MainStreetAiStrategy) alongside unchanged Greedy/Random.
- Cases: (a) hoards (end-turn with actionsRemaining>0) when an unaffordable high-value hand/market target exists, (b) spends when no valuable unaffordable target, (c) at bankedActions==2 returns spend (bank value 0), (d) respects enumerateLegalActions legality (no illegal action emitted), (e) difficulty scaling — Easy spends where Hard hoards on same state.
- Existing ai-action-budget + monte-carlo tests remain green (or drift documented).
- `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New suite targets `BankingGreedyStrategy`; GreedyStrategy and RandomStrategy remain importable/unchanged.
2. Deterministic hoard vs spend vs cap vs legality cases covered (a–d above).
3. Difficulty scaling test: same state, Easy spends where Hard hoards (or quantified threshold difference documented).
4. No regression in existing ai-action-budget / monte-carlo tests (or documented drift).

## Minimal Implementation
- Retarget/create helper makeState({hand, market, coins, banked, difficulty/config}) in tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts.
- Table-driven tests for cases above; include helper to build MainStreetState with hand/market/business+upgrade/event cards and bankedActions.
- Run: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
None (test-first — blocks F2).

## Deliverables
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (expanded/retargeted)
- Passing unit run for touched file

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Main Street only; no core-engine changes.
- Do not modify GreedyStrategy behaviour in this slice — tests define the contract it must satisfy in F2.

# Feature: Hybrid Look-Ahead and Difficulty Scaling

## Summary
Extend scoreBankOption to hybrid visible + pipeline look-ahead (top-N market/deck cards) with look-ahead depth/aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Easy < Medium < Hard) via aiPlanningHorizon() horizon factor.

## Target Outcome
BankingGreedyStrategy considers both visible unaffordable targets and anticipated near-future targets; Easy hoards less/deeper look-ahead than Hard.

## Definition of Done
- Heuristic considers (a) visible unaffordable targets (hand + market row) and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline (top-K deck or market pipeline inspection; bounded to depth).
- Look-ahead depth reduced at lower difficulties (proposed defaults: Easy 0–1, Medium 2–3, Hard 4 — documented in comments; adjust if state.market.deck shape differs).
- Factors: bankedActions, targetCost vs coins (closeness = 1 - gap/cost), aiPlanningHorizon() horizon/cap, bankHeadroom = (2-banked)/2; tuning thresholds documented (closeness < 0.05 -> 0, raw < 1 -> 0).
- Easy hoards strictly less than Hard on shared state (F1 difficulty test passes); no over-hoard at cap; pipeline empty/unavailable falls back to visible-only without crash.
- npm run build + unit tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Hybrid heuristic (visible + pipeline look-ahead) implemented with difficulty-gated depth.
2. Difficulty scaling: Easy look-ahead/aggressiveness < Hard (same state, different decision documented and tested).
3. All factors (banked, closeness, horizon/cap, headroom) applied; tuning documented in comments.
4. Fallback: empty pipeline does not throw; visible-only valuation still works.

## Minimal Implementation
- Add helper getLookAheadTargets(state, depth): reads state.market.deck / pipeline or equivalent (inspect MainStreetState first); bounded to depth; returns Business/Upgrade/Event cards with value estimate.
- Make scoreBankOption(state, difficulty?) accept optional DifficultyName (defaults to state.config.difficultyName or Medium); map difficulty -> {depth, aggressivenessMultiplier}.
- BankingGreedyStrategy passes difficulty through to scoreBankOption; apply multiplier to final bank score.
- Wire tests to pass difficulty explicitly for deterministic coverage.

## Dependencies
- F2: Additive BankingGreedyStrategy core (needs BankingGreedyStrategy + scoreBankOption gate to extend).

## Deliverables
- Updated scoreBankOption + getLookAheadTargets helpers in MainStreetAiStrategy.ts with difficulty scaling
- Inline comments explaining depth map and tuning thresholds
- F1 difficulty test passing at hard vs easy extremes

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` (read pipeline shape)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` (market/deck pipeline)
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Keep look-ahead narrow (few cards, top of deck/pipeline); if pipeline shape is unavailable or look-ahead proves noisy, narrow to visible with documented fallback and OPEN QUESTION.
- Main Street only.

## Target Outcome
Monte Carlo harness exposes BankingGreedyStrategy as a first-class, selectable strategy variant without replacing the existing greedy baseline.

## Definition of Done
- MonteCarloStrategy union extended with 'banking-greedy'; ALL_STRATEGIES includes it.
- createAiPlayerForStrategy('banking-greedy', seed, difficulty?) returns new MainStreetAiPlayer(new BankingGreedyStrategy(difficulty), rng); existing 'greedy' path still returns pure GreedyStrategy (verified by win-rate / action-type divergence test or strategy-name assertion).
